title: The potential of artificial intelligence to improve patient safety: a scoping review
explain_beginner: Researchers reviewed nearly 400 studies to understand how artificial intelligence could make hospitals safer for patients. They examined eight major types of medical errors and injuries, from infections to missed diagnoses. The review found that AI could help predict and prevent many of these problems, especially by using new technologies like wearable devices and sensors to monitor patients. AI seems most promising for catching drug problems, sudden patient decline, and diagnostic mistakes where current methods fall short.
explain_business: This review demonstrates substantial commercial and clinical opportunity in deploying AI for patient safety monitoring across hospitals. Investment should prioritize applications addressing drug safety, patient deterioration detection, and diagnostic support, where AI can meaningfully outperform existing approaches. Implementation requires integrating sensor technologies and monitoring devices with AI analytics platforms. The convergence of clinical need, preventability, and high economic impact of these three harm categories presents the strongest business case for healthcare technology vendors and providers.
explain_practitioner: A scoping review of 392 studies examined AI applications across eight adverse event domains in healthcare. Researchers systematically searched MEDLINE and synthesized literature narratively for each domain, evaluating AI potential based on incidence, cost, and preventability. Novel data sources included vital sign monitors, wearables, pressure sensors, and computer vision. Results indicated AI shows greatest promise in adverse drug events, decompensation, and diagnostic errors, where current prevention strategies are limited and multimodal data integration enables superior predictive accuracy.
